response.title: which power station runs christmas lights for the most nights
response.answer:
For running Christmas lights over multiple nights, the best power station is the one with the most usable battery capacity (Wh), not necessarily the highest wattage (W).

If you're using LED Christmas lights for 6 hours per night, a large power station can potentially last several weeks without recharging.

The key factors are:

Battery capacity (Wh): Determines how many nights your lights can run.

Light consumption (W): LED string lights use much less electricity than incandescent lights.

Inverter efficiency: Using a standard AC outlet typically loses 10–20% of the battery's energy.

Standby consumption: Some power stations consume significant energy just keeping the AC outlets active.

## Power stations that last the most nights

Assuming 50W of LED Christmas lights running 6 hours per night, with 80% usable battery energy:

| Power station | Battery capacity | Estimated nights |
|---|---:|---:|
| EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X | 12,288Wh | **32 nights** |
| EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra | 6,144Wh | 16 nights |
| Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus | 5,040Wh | 13 nights |
| Anker SOLIX F3800 | 3,840Wh | 10 nights |
| EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra | 3,072Wh | 8 nights |

These are simplified estimates; AC standby consumption can substantially reduce runtime, especially with low-power lights. Capacities are based on published specifications. <Cite refs={["turn528234search3","turn528234search0","turn528234search17"]}/>
